title: 10/31 시험 기출
intro: 2026년 10월 31일 실제 시험(난이도 4)에 나온 주제 묶음입니다: 자기소개 · 집/방 묘사 · 서점(particular 책) · 골프 · 새로운 이웃 · 기념 휴일, 롤플레이는 골프장 추천(질문하기 → 문제 해결 → 관련 경험). 주제는 실제 기출이고, 질문 문장은 그 주제로 자주 나오는 형태로 만든 예상 질문입니다. 모범답안의 '나'는 이날 서베이에 맞춰 '분당 아파트에 혼자 살고, 지금은 일을 하지 않음, 여가: 독서 · 골프 · 조깅 · 카페 · 영화 · TV'로 통일했습니다. 서베이를 이번과 같게 고르면 이 답안을 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
strategy: 자기소개에서 말한 소재(혼자 사는 집 · 서현역 서점 · 골프 연습장 · 탄천 조깅)를 다른 문제에서 그대로 다시 쓰세요.
서점 · 골프는 설문 주제라 묘사 → 루틴 → 경험 콤보로 나옵니다. 경험 질문은 반드시 과거시제로 말하세요.
새로운 이웃 · 기념 휴일은 돌발 주제로, 롤플레이는 골프장 추천 상황으로 나왔습니다. 롤플레이는 질문 3개 이상 → 사과 + 대안 2~3개 → 과거 경험 순서를 지키세요. 옆집 박 할머니, 위층 새 부부, 대전 부모님 댁 추석처럼 이야기 하나씩을 정해 두면 당황하지 않아요.
난이도 4는 IM2~IH를 노리는 구간입니다. IM3 답안을 먼저 입에 붙이고, 여유가 생기면 IH 디테일을 한두 문장씩 더하세요.

I'm a calm person, and I like quiet places. In my free time, I read books, go jogging, and play golf. On weekends, I often go to a bookstore or a cafe near my place. Living alone is really comfortable, and I enjoy my own time. Yeah, that's a little bit about me.

Living alone can feel a little quiet at times, but I've come to love the freedom of having my own space. I think this lifestyle really suits me right now. Yeah, that's pretty much who I am.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you live alone in a house or an apartment. Describe your home to me. What does it look like, and how many rooms does it have?
questions.ko: 설문에서 주택이나 아파트에 혼자 산다고 하셨습니다. 집을 묘사해 주세요. 어떻게 생겼고, 방은 몇 개인가요?
tips: 10/31 기출 주제: 집 묘사. 서베이 '홀로 거주'에서 나온 문제입니다.
위치(분당 · 몇 층) → 크기 · 방 개수 → 방마다 한 문장 → 좋아하는 점 → 마무리. There is / There are 를 꼭 쓰세요.

questions.ko: 서점에 가면 보통 무엇을 하나요? 처음부터 끝까지 평소 방문 과정을 설명해 주세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you what I usually do at the bookstore. I usually go there on weekday afternoons because it's not crowded. First, I check the bestseller section near the entrance. Then, I go to the novel section and look around for a while. If I find an interesting book, I sit at the big table and read a few pages. After that, I usually buy one or two books. Sometimes I also buy a coffee at the cafe inside. I usually stay there for about two hours. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the bookstore.
answers.IH: Okay, let me walk you through a typical visit to the bookstore. Since I'm not working right now, I usually go there on weekday afternoons when it's nice and quiet. The first thing I do is check the bestseller list near the entrance to see what people are reading these days. After that, I head straight to the fiction section, because I'm a big fan of mystery novels. When a book catches my eye, I take it to the big wooden table and read the first chapter. If it hooks me, I buy it, and if not, I just put it back and keep looking. I also like to stop by the stationery corner and look at notebooks and pens, even though I don't really need them. Before I leave, I usually grab an iced americano at the cafe inside. All in all, I end up staying there for two or three hours without even noticing. Yeah, that's how a typical visit goes for me.
answers.AL: Okay, let me walk you through what a typical bookstore visit looks like for me. Since I'm not working at the moment, I usually go on a weekday afternoon, when the place is quiet and I can actually find a seat. I always start at the bestseller display by the entrance, just to get a sense of what people are into these days. Then I make my way to the fiction section, because I'm a sucker for mystery novels. My rule is pretty simple: if a book catches my eye, I read the first chapter at the big wooden table before deciding. If the story grabs me, I buy it right away, but if it doesn't, I put it back without any guilt. Along the way, I usually wander into the stationery corner and end up buying a notebook I definitely don't need. Before heading home, I treat myself to an iced americano at the little cafe inside and flip through my new book. Before I know it, two or three hours have flown by. For me, it's not just shopping, it's more like a small ritual that recharges me. Yeah, that's pretty much how my bookstore visits go.

tips: 10/31 기출 주제: 골프. 연습장 · 스크린골프 · 필드 세 곳을 묘사하고, 좋아하는 이유 두 가지로 마무리하세요.
driving range(연습장), screen golf(스크린골프), golf course(필드), tee time(예약 시간)을 익혀 두세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about playing golf. I started playing golf about two years ago. I usually practice at a driving range near my apartment. It's only a 10-minute drive from my place. Sometimes I also play screen golf with my friends. A few times a year, we go to a real golf course outside the city. I like golf because I can enjoy nature and get some exercise. Also, it's a great way to spend time with my friends. Yeah, that's why I love playing golf.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about golf, which is my favorite sport these days. I picked it up about two years ago when a friend of mine dragged me to a driving range. Now I practice at a driving range near my apartment, just a 10-minute drive away. It's a three-story building with a big green net, and there are about fifty booths. When the weather is bad, my friends and I play screen golf instead, which is really popular in Korea. A few times a year, we also book a tee time at a real golf course in Yongin. What I like most about golf is that it's just me and the ball, so I can really focus. Plus, walking on the green grass under the open sky is so refreshing. It's not a cheap sport, but I think it's totally worth it. Yeah, that's why golf is such a big part of my life now.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about golf, because it's pretty much my favorite thing to do these days. I got into it about two years ago, when a friend practically dragged me to a driving range, and I've been hooked ever since. These days, I practice at a driving range about 10 minutes from my apartment by car. It's a huge three-story building surrounded by a giant green net, with around fifty booths facing the field. When the weather doesn't cooperate, my friends and I go for screen golf instead, which is a really big thing in Korea. And a few times a year, we book a tee time at a real course in Yongin, which always feels like a special occasion. What I love most about golf is that it's just you and the ball, so it forces me to slow down and focus. On top of that, walking across the green fairway under a wide-open sky clears my head like nothing else. Of course, it can be frustrating, and my score is still nothing to brag about. It's also a pretty expensive hobby, but I honestly think every penny is worth it. Yeah, that's why golf has become such a big part of my life.

questions.en: Tell me about your routine when you practice golf. What do you do before, during, and after practice?
questions.ko: 골프 연습할 때의 루틴을 말해 주세요. 연습 전, 연습 중, 연습 후에 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 10/31 기출 주제: 골프. 전 → 중 → 후 세 단계로 나누어 말하면 루틴 질문이 쉬워집니다.
about three times a week, usually, always, After that 같은 빈도 · 순서 표현을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my golf routine. I go to the driving range about three times a week. I usually go in the morning because it's not busy. First, I stretch for about five minutes. Then, I hit about two hundred balls for an hour. I start with short clubs and finish with the driver. After practice, I check my swing videos on my phone. Then I go home and take a shower. Yeah, that's my usual golf routine.
answers.IH: Okay, let me walk you through my golf routine. I go to the driving range about three times a week, usually in the morning when it's quiet. Before I start, I always stretch my shoulders and back for about five minutes, because I hurt my back once. Then I warm up with short wedge shots and slowly move up to the longer irons. I always save the driver for last, since that's the most fun part. In total, I hit around two hundred balls in an hour. While I practice, I record my swing on my phone so I can check what I'm doing wrong. After that, I often go to the putting green and practice short putts for about twenty minutes. When I get home, I watch my swing videos and compare them with golf lessons on YouTube. Yeah, that's pretty much my golf routine.
answers.AL: Okay, let me walk you through my golf routine, because I'm actually pretty strict about it. I hit the driving range about three times a week, usually first thing in the morning, when it's nice and empty. Before I even touch a club, I spend about five minutes stretching my shoulders and lower back, since I strained my back once and learned my lesson. Then I warm up with short wedge shots and gradually work my way up to the longer irons. I always save the driver for last, because, let's be honest, smashing the ball as far as I can is the most satisfying part. All in all, I go through around two hundred balls in about an hour. While I'm practicing, I set up my phone on a little tripod and record my swing from the side. Once I'm done with full swings, I head over to the putting green and spend another twenty minutes on short putts, which is where most of my strokes are wasted. Later at home, I go over the videos and compare my swing with lessons on YouTube. It might sound a bit obsessive, but seeing even a small improvement makes it all worth it. Yeah, that's pretty much my golf routine.

그날 저녁엔 잡채, 온갖 전, 생선구이로 잔치를 벌였고, 저는 확실히 너무 많이 먹었어요.
저녁을 먹고 옛 동네를 산책하며 커다란 보름달을 올려다봤어요.
조용히 부모님 건강을 빌었는데, 왠지 좀 뭉클해졌어요.
혼자 살면 그런 따뜻함을 자주 느끼지 못해서, 그 주말이 마음을 가득 채워 줬어요.
네, 그게 제가 가장 기억하는 명절이에요.

questions.en: How have holidays in your country changed compared to the past? What are some of the differences?
questions.ko: 당신 나라의 명절은 예전과 비교해 어떻게 달라졌나요? 어떤 차이가 있나요?
tips: 10/31 기출 주제: 기념 휴일 (14~15번 고난도 비교 · 변화 유형 대비).
In the past / When I was a kid → But these days → 내 생각(좋은 점 · 아쉬운 점) 순서로 used to, compared to 를 쓰세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me talk about how holidays have changed. In the past, holidays were all about family. Everyone went to their hometown, and big families got together. Women used to cook a lot of food for many days. But these days, things are very different. Many people travel abroad during long holidays. Also, families buy food instead of cooking everything at home. I think holidays are more relaxing now compared to the past. Yeah, that's how holidays have changed in Korea.
answers.IH: Okay, let me talk about how holidays have changed in Korea. When I was a kid, holidays were all about big family gatherings. Dozens of relatives used to come to my grandparents' house, and we stayed there for three days. The women in the family spent days cooking food for the ancestral rites, which was really hard work. But these days, things have changed a lot. Families are smaller, and many people just meet their parents for one day. Also, more and more people buy ready-made food or skip the rites altogether. On top of that, a lot of people use long holidays to travel abroad or simply rest at home. I think it's a good change, because holidays are less stressful now than they used to be. But at the same time, I sometimes miss the noisy, crowded holidays of my childhood. Yeah, that's how holidays have changed.
answers.AL: Okay, let me talk about how holidays have changed in Korea, because the difference is pretty striking. When I was a kid, holidays meant one thing: huge family gatherings. Dozens of relatives would pack into my grandparents' house, and we'd spend all three days there together. Behind the scenes, though, the women in the family were stuck in the kitchen for days, preparing food for the ancestral rites, which was honestly exhausting for them. Fast forward to today, and things look completely different. Families have gotten smaller, and a lot of people just visit their parents for a day and head back home. More and more families also buy ready-made holiday food, or even skip the rites altogether. On top of that, the airports are packed during long holidays, because people would rather travel abroad or simply recharge at home. Overall, I think it's a healthy change, since holidays have become much less of a burden compared to the past, especially for women. That said, I do miss the noisy, crowded holidays of my childhood sometimes. Yeah, that's how holidays have changed over the years.

IM3: 명절이 어떻게 달라졌는지 말해 볼게요.
예전에는 명절이 온통 가족 중심이었어요.
모두 고향에 갔고, 대가족이 모였어요.
여자들은 며칠 동안 음식을 잔뜩 만들곤 했어요.

긴 연휴에 해외여행을 가는 사람이 많아요.

예전에 비해 지금 명절이 더 여유로운 것 같아요.

집안 여자들은 차례 음식을 만드느라 며칠을 보냈는데, 정말 힘든 일이었어요.
하지만 요즘은 많이 달라졌어요.
가족 규모가 작아졌고, 부모님을 하루만 뵙고 오는 사람도 많아요.
또 완성된 음식을 사거나 차례를 아예 생략하는 사람도 점점 늘고 있어요.
게다가 긴 연휴에 해외여행을 가거나 그냥 집에서 쉬는 사람도 많아요.
명절이 예전보다 스트레스가 덜해서 좋은 변화라고 생각해요.
그래도 가끔은 어린 시절의 시끌벅적하고 북적이던 명절이 그리워요.
네, 이게 명절이 달라진 모습이에요.
AL: 한국 명절이 어떻게 달라졌는지 말해 볼게요, 차이가 꽤 뚜렷하거든요.
제가 어릴 때 명절은 딱 하나, 대가족 모임을 뜻했어요.
친척 수십 명이 할머니 할아버지 댁에 꽉 들어차서 사흘 내내 함께 지냈어요.
그런데 그 뒤에서는 집안 여자들이 차례 음식을 준비하느라 며칠씩 부엌에 묶여 있었는데, 솔직히 정말 고된 일이었어요.
지금으로 넘어오면 모습이 완전히 달라요.
가족 규모가 작아졌고, 많은 사람이 부모님을 하루만 뵙고 집으로 돌아가요.
명절 음식을 사 오거나 아예 차례를 생략하는 집도 점점 늘고 있어요.
게다가 사람들이 해외여행을 가거나 그냥 집에서 재충전하는 걸 더 원해서 긴 연휴엔 공항이 꽉 차요.
전반적으로 예전에 비해 명절이 특히 여성들에게 훨씬 덜 부담스러워져서 건강한 변화라고 생각해요.
그렇긴 해도 어린 시절의 시끌벅적하고 북적이던 명절이 가끔 정말 그리워요.
네, 이게 세월이 흐르며 명절이 달라진 모습이에요.
